mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has shown consistent week-on-week improvement from -17.1% to -13.6% over four weeks, indicating a steady recovery trend. This monotonic improvement will continue, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks relative to the baseline period.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 3.5 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the prior 28 days, or reverses to decline week-on-week for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has stabilized near -12% over the last two weeks, indicating workplace return has plateaued. This plateau signals behavioral resistance to further commuting increases, which will suppress retail recovery as discretionary spending remains constrained by work-from-home persistence.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES change < 1 percentage point week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the prior 28-day mean despite WORKPLACES remaining flat or declining further.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has recovered from -11.1% to near zero (-0.9%), indicating outdoor activity normalization. This outdoor substitution effect will reduce pressure on indoor retail-and-recreation venues, causing RETAIL_REC to remain depressed or decline further as consumers redirect discretionary time outdoors.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -2% and remains positive for one week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -11.1% to -0.9% over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases despite PARKS remaining above -2%, indicating outdoor substitution is not suppressing indoor retail.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility remains severely depressed at -35.3%, indicating public transportation avoidance persists. This transit collapse constrains retail accessibility for non-car-dependent populations, preventing RETAIL_REC from recovering beyond current levels over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -30% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -35.3% (t-0w), showing no recovery trend
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 2 percentage points over the next 28 days while TRANSIT remains below -30%.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has stabilized near -3.4%, indicating essential shopping patterns are locked in. Coupled with RESIDENTIAL remaining elevated at 5.6%, this signals consumers are consolidating trips and minimizing discretionary retail visits, suppressing RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM change < 0.5 percentage points and RESIDENTIAL > 5% simultaneously
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 3 percentage points over the next 28 days despite GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL remaining in observed ranges.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined from 8.0% to 5.6% over four weeks, indicating gradual return to normal commuting patterns. If this trend continues and RESIDENTIAL falls below 5%, it will signal policy-driven reopening acceleration, triggering a corresponding acceleration in RETAIL_REC recovery over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 5% in the next two weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined 2.4 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL falls below 5% but RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The convergence of PARKS near zero, WORKPLACES stabilized, and RETAIL_REC improving suggests a seasonal transition into fall with normalized outdoor activity and workplace routines. This seasonal normalization will drive RETAIL_REC higher as back-to-school and fall shopping patterns activate over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS within -2% to +2% AND WORKPLACES change < 1 percentage point week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days despite PARKS and WORKPLACES meeting convergence conditions.

If TRANSIT does not recover by more than 5 percentage points within one week, this car-dependent recovery will plateau, preventing RETAIL_REC from exceeding -10% over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT fails to improve by more than 5 percentage points in the next week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -35.3% with minimal week-on-week change
